Continued strong execution drives another quarterof sustained growth
21 July 2026 - Compass Group PLC, a global leader in food services, today announces trading results for the third quarter ended 30 June 2026.
Strong performance
The Group delivered another strong quarter, with organic revenue growth of 7.1%. Net new business growth accelerated into our 4 - 5% target range as expected, and we remain on track to deliver net new growth at this level for the fifth consecutive year.
Client retention remained excellent at 96% and our pipeline of opportunities continues to support confidence in future growth. Like-for-like growth was in line with our expectations, with volumes in North America benefiting modestly from the Football World Cup. In International, like-for-like growth moderated, reflecting lower inflation and Sports & Leisure calendar timings.

Continued strong growth momentum
The fragmented $360bn outsourcing food services market remains highly attractive. Compass continues to capture a significant share of this large and growing opportunity. Over the last 12 months, the Group secured $4.3bn2 of new business wins, up 16% year-on-year, with 50% of new business wins from first time outsourcing.
Business & Industry remains our strongest performing sector, delivering double-digit organic growth and generating more than $2bn2 of new business across different industries. We continue to support leading AI hyperscalers across the data centre ecosystem, providing food and support services across both construction and operational phases, leveraging our expertise in complex, infrastructure-intensive environments.
Sports & Leisure in our International region continues to grow strongly, with a significant contribution from first-time outsourcing, highlighting the sizeable opportunity in an underpenetrated market as venues invest to elevate the fan experience and unlock the full commercial potential of their operations.
Education continues to build momentum following a record selling season across K-12 and Higher Education. The recent University of Kentucky win, our largest in the sector to date, highlights the growing demand for integrated solutions across campus and healthcare environments, further demonstrating the power of our sectorisation strategy, with multiple Compass brands working together at scale.
Healthcare & Senior Living continues to represent a significant long-term opportunity. In North America, six of our top 20 new business wins this year were in the sector, reflecting the strength of our sectorised approach and differentiated proposition.
Defence, Offshore & Remote continues to benefit from increased investment in defence and energy infrastructure, underpinned by our expertise in delivering essential services in remote and logistically demanding locations.
Investing in growth
Whilst capex is trending around 3.5% of sales for the year to date, we expect this percentage to be slightly elevated at full year due to the timing of client mobilisations.
The Group's net expenditure on M&A was $2.4bn for the year to date, broadly unchanged from its position at the half year.
Reiterating 2026 guidance
Strong execution and continued growth momentum gives us confidence in delivering underlying operating profit growth of above 11% in constant currency. This is driven by:
·
Around 7% organic revenue growth
·
Around 2% profit growth from M&A
·
Ongoing margin progression
Dominic Blakemore, CEO of Compass Group, said:
"Our business continues to perform strongly, driven by the strength of our sector-focused model, disciplined execution and resilient client demand. We are winning market share across multiple sectors, supported by the strongest pipeline of opportunities we have ever seen.
With an addressable market exceeding $360bn and significant opportunities to further increase penetration, we remain confident in delivering another year of strong earnings growth and continued margin progression."
Currency
If current spot rates were to continue for the remainder of the year, foreign exchange translation would positively impact 2025 revenue by $438m3 and operating profit by $23m3.

About Compass Group PLC
Compass Group is a global leader in food services, operating in over 25 countries, with over 590,000 employees worldwide and generating underlying revenues of over $46bn for the 2025 fiscal year. Our core focus is the provision of outsourced food services and targeted support services. Compass Group operates across five sectors: Business & Industry, Healthcare & Senior Living, Education, Sports & Leisure, and Defence, Offshore & Remote, using a portfolio of bespoke B2B brands.

COMPASS GROUP PLC (the "Company")
STERLING EQUIVALENT OF INTERIM DIVIDEND
The Company announced on 11 May 2026 that the Board had approved an interim dividend for the financial year ending 30 September 2026 of 25.5 US cents per ordinary share payable on 30 July 2026.
The Company, today, announces that the Sterling equivalent of the interim dividend is 19.0 pence per ordinary share based on an exchange rate of US$1=£0.747.
The US$:£ conversion rate was determined by the actual rates achieved by the Company buying forward contracts for Sterling currency, during the five working days preceding this announcement, for delivery ahead of the dividend payment date on 30 July 2026.

company_30s.what_they_do: Compass Group runs a global catering and support‑services business.  They provide food, facilities and support services to schools, hospitals, universities, corporate offices and government sites, delivering meals, maintenance and other back‑of‑house functions.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The company serves a huge, essential market – anyone who needs regular food or facility support.  Its global footprint gives it a stable revenue stream, and its long‑term contracts with public institutions provide predictable cash flow that many investors value.
company_30s.current_state: Compass Group is in a steady growth phase.  It recently shifted the currency in which its ordinary shares trade from pounds to U.S. dollars, a change aimed at attracting more international investors.  Earnings are solid, dividends are being paid, and the company is maintaining its global service network.

rns_narrative: The company has been busy tightening its corporate governance – board and committee changes, an AGM that refreshed the share structure, and a block‑listing review to manage large‑holder influence.

Financially, it has released a series of results updates – Q1 and Q3 trading statements, a half‑year review, and a dividend announcement – all showing steady performance and a modest but consistent payout.

A notable operational tweak is the currency conversion of its shares from pounds to dollars, signalling a strategic move to align with global capital markets and reduce currency risk for overseas investors.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Cautious optimism as the company realigns its currency and keeps earnings stable.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls point to Compass Group’s long‑term contracts, steady dividend, and global brand.  They see the currency switch as a positive step that could broaden the investor base.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the shift to dollars could expose the company to foreign‑exchange swings and that block‑listing changes might dilute shareholder power.  They also note that the stock has already fallen sharply, raising concerns about whether the fundamentals can support a rebound.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Recent posts are largely bullish after the Q3 update, but overall engagement is low.  The community is watching for the next earnings call to confirm whether the fundamentals will sustain the upside.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends shows no recent interest – a classic contrarian sign that the market has forgotten the stock, leaving room for a surprise bounce.

near_term_catalysts: The upcoming Q3 earnings release – if the company beats revenue or margin expectations, it could spark a sharp price rally.
A potential share‑buyback or dividend hike announced in the next trading update would signal confidence and improve per‑share metrics.
A spike in trading volume at the 200‑day moving‑average support level could confirm that buyers are returning after capitulation.
expect_next.watch_for: Key signals to confirm the thesis are: (1) a volume surge above the 50‑day average, (2) a clear reversal in the 20‑day moving average, and (3) management’s comment that the currency change is improving liquidity and investor sentiment.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock is likely in the early recovery phase of a deep crash cycle.  If the APEX score is high (tight compression) and volume dries out, a mean‑reversion bounce is plausible within the next 2–3 months.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: Compass Group has suffered a deep price plunge, but its core business remains strong and its cash flow is healthy.  Historically, such deep crashes in the catering sector have rebounded sharply once the market recognises the company’s stable contracts and global presence.  If the stock recovers to roughly the midpoint of its 52‑week range, upside could be 2–3× the current level.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The biggest risk is currency volatility from the dollar conversion and potential dilution from the block‑listing review.  A sudden drop in global food costs or a slowdown in public‑sector contracts could also blunt the bounce.  The worst‑case scenario is a further 10–15% decline if the market remains wary of the currency shift.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside: 200–300% if the stock reaches the 50‑week midpoint.  Potential downside: 70–80% if the market remains in a prolonged bearish stance.  The asymmetry is strongly in favour of the long side.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a clear volume spike at the 200‑day support, with a stop just below that support.  Allocate 10–15% of discretionary capital per position and use a trailing stop once the price moves 10% higher.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash or a small position until the Q3 earnings call.  Watch for a positive earnings surprise or a dividend announcement.  If either occurs and volume confirms, consider a quick entry.
playbook.if_passing: No terminal risks are evident, so the default stance is bullish.  Only consider exiting if the company announces a major restructuring or faces regulatory action that could impair its core services.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Compass Group’s deep price drop, combined with a strategic currency shift and solid earnings, creates a high‑reward contrarian opportunity that could see the stock rebound sharply once volume confirms the mean‑reversion.
